title: Different test, different score
hook: Easy and hard toy tasks have fixed accuracy rates; change the assessment mix.

knows: basic arithmetic and how to compare two stated rules
doesNotKnow: how to explain why changing task difficulty changes the aggregate without measuring learning potential

misconception: A lower score under a harder task mix establishes reduced ability to learn.
objective: Explain why changing task difficulty changes the aggregate without measuring learning potential.

claims.text: Mindset challenges treating present performance as a fixed limit on what someone can learn.

claims.text: Original stipulated toy: Invented expected accuracies 100% and 50%; independent item expectations; fractional expected correct items; not an observed experiment. Exact selection inputs [{"label": "Mostly easy", "values": [8, 100, 2, 50]}, {"label": "Mostly hard", "values": [2, 100, 8, 50]}]; second author arithmetic check A=90, B=60. Mostly easy yields {A}%; mostly hard {B}%. Only task weights change; neither group’s assumed accuracy changes.
claims.source: EDD-010-books-100-models.md formula; this brief fixes invented inputs, not sampled people or measured outcomes. Independent arithmetic recomputation recorded in answerCheck. claims.text: Does it hold up? These invented scores measure no mindset intervention or future learning capacity.
